Helping a real estate brand show up consistently

A practical content plan for Instagram, Facebook, TikTok and LinkedIn, without turning every post into a property listing.

My role

I handled social strategy, content planning, captions, publishing and community responses across four platforms.

Sector

Real estate · Ongoing engagement

Status

Case study / reported evidence

Topics

Real estate · Multi-platform · Ongoing

01 / Starting point

The challenge

The business needed to stay visible online, but a feed full of property listings alone would not give people many reasons to follow it. The plan also had to work across four different platforms.

The insight

Someone considering a property needs confidence in the people behind it. Useful information and a consistent presence can help build that confidence over time.

02 / The approach

The plan

  • Build a manageable schedule of roughly 10 to 15 posts per month.
  • Adapt the message and format to each platform instead of posting the exact same thing everywhere.
  • Balance property content with posts that help people understand the brand and its work.
03 / Execution

Make the rhythm visible.

Content direction

I chose content themes that could build familiarity and trust rather than focusing entirely on listings.

Calendar and captions

I planned roughly 10 to 15 posts a month, with copy suited to Instagram, Facebook, TikTok and LinkedIn.

Publishing and replies

I published posts and managed community responses across the four channels.

Checking progress

I used platform data to see what people responded to. I did not count views or comments as property visits or sales.

04 / Results

Evidence with the label still attached.

A supplied 90-day snapshot reports 9,822 Facebook views (+45.4%), 554 content interactions (+129.9%) and 3,152 viewers (+45.9%). These are platform engagement indicators, not qualified buyer enquiries, site visits or sales. Exact snapshot dates and exports must be verified before public use.

05 / Reflection

What stays after the campaign?

A steady content plan can be more useful than posting constantly. The next step is to connect social activity more closely to genuine buyer enquiries and visits.
